business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual IBAN Issuance and Digital Wallet Reserve Management

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama; national unitary jurisdiction without sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Commercial Code and General Corporation Law, with common-law-style corporate flexibility in practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (effective 2012, including investment chapter)
ICSID Convention (Panama is a Contracting State)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 2015 (prevention of money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing; creation of the Registro de Titulares de Derecho for legal entities), as implemented by Decreto Ejecutivo No. 155 de 2017; supervision by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and, for licensed payment/electronic money institutions, the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the beneficial owner passport (biographic page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Civil Registry of the beneficial owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority in the country of origin; if not a Hague Convention member, consular legalization through a Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate documents of any corporate shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of no prior registration from Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama if the receiving authority requires international authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney to the Panamanian resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian notary if executed in Panama; if executed abroad, notary of the foreign jurisdiction followed by apostille or consular legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization for foreign-granted authorities; no additional authentication for domestic Panamanian notarized instruments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Panamanian national sanctions and FIU watchlists; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) in accordance with FATF recommendations; source-of-funds verification and ongoing transaction monitoring required for regulated electronic money institutions classified as high-risk special license.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Legal Registry and Name Reservation Portal (Sistema de Registro en Línea / RPP)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use Spanish or another language written in Latin alphabetic characters; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters in the filed instrument. All Panamanian stock corporations must include the suffix 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima'. The proposed name must be distinguishable from existing names, must not imply governmental or sovereign status, and must not mislead as to regulated financial activity without prior grant of the relevant license.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registered agent receives the registry note listing grounds for refusal. The applicant may file a written 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Dirección General del Registro Público within ten (10) business days from notification; if reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an 'Recurso de Apelación' before the superior administrative body and ultimately a 'Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa' before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice of Panama. The resident agent should confirm the current appeal form and fee schedule before filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A standard Panamanian S.A. may use the resident agent's office as its registered address for non-operational holding purposes. A licensed Electronic Money Institution must maintain a genuine physical operational presence in Panama, including a local compliance function, board-meeting capability, business records, and risk-management infrastructure; a purely virtual office is not acceptable for the EMI license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk: approximately 85-90% probability of unannounced on-site examination for a licensed EMI by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá and/or the Unidad de Análisis Financiero during the first two years; approximately 15-20% probability for a dormant or purely holding S.A. with no regulated activity and no local operations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registry submission and initial corporate KYC file set-up
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark plus administrative cost under Executive Decree 155 of 2017

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening plus enhanced due diligence for UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for structured PEP, OFAC and UN sanctions database screening

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Panama General Corporation Law), as amended, particularly arts. 1-119; Ley 4 de 2009 (electronic registry procedure); Ley 15 de 2021 and SBP implementing rules for electronic-money institutions; beneficial-owner filing under Ley 52 de 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General, Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantil)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Social y Estatutos (constitutive charter) submitted for inscription as the Aviso de Constitución / Escritura de Constitución
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama S.A. legislation does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up equity or an escrow-account rule at formation; the charter must state authorized capital (commonly US$10,000). For the e-money licence, the SBP requires minimum paid-in capital and a safeguarding arrangement under which issued electronic money is backed by liquid reserve assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Company's charter, submitted as Pacto Social y Estatutos, is approved and the authorized capital is declared fully subscribed; share certificates are directed to be issued to the inaugural shareholders. (2) The registered office is fixed at the address appearing in the charter in Panama City. (3) The directors and the President, Secretary and Treasurer named in the charter are formally appointed as officers. (4) The officers are authorized to pay registry fees, open bank accounts, and retain the resident agent. (5) A Chief Compliance Officer is appointed for AML and electronic-money licensing, with authority to prepare and submit the SBP authorization application and corporate governance policies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability reservation and corporate object certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Certificación de Nombre (online/notary window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the resident agent/notary to request a certified name availability check. The proposed name must include 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.' and avoid prohibited banking terms unless licensed. The corporate object must explicitly recite electronic-money issuance, e-wallet management and payment services to enable the SBP license.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit a revised name request or file reconsideration with the Registro Público; formal written re-presentation cures any administrative query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarized execution of Pacto Social y Estatutos
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public authorized in the judicial circuit of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the incorporators or their attorney-in-fact sign the Spanish-language charter before the notary. The notarized document must set out the corporate name, duration, domicile, object, authorized capital, directors, officers, resident agent and share clauses. Certify signature and pagination before onward registry filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney for the incorporator
List of proposed officers and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct typographical or legal defects by notarial addendum (adenda) and re-certify; if refused, execute a fresh charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized first-copy and one protocolized copy with the required registration form and payment of official fees. The registry performs a legal review and issues the inscription/entry number, converting the company into a valid Sociedad Anónima as of the registration date.
required_dossiers: Apostille or legalization if charter executed abroad
Power of attorney for filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any 'vista' or defect within the registry's stated term; pay omitted tariffs and re-file; an unfavourable denial may be appealed to the higher administrative instance of the Registro Público.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate books, resident agent confirmation and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident agent and Registro Público de Panamá (Personas Jurídicas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the statutory corporate ledger, shareholder register and share-certificate stock book with the resident agent. File the notice of beneficial owner under Ley 52 de 2016 if the company is not exempt, and obtain an updated Persona Jurídica certificate confirming directors and officers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify missing entries or signatures and resubmit; make a late-filing cure with penalty payment before enforcement action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NIT/RUC registration and municipal business operation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipality of the registered office (e.g. Municipio de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the registry certificate to apply for the company's NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). File the municipal Aviso de Operación and occupational health notice for the administrative office; identify the regulated EMI license as the business activity.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of physical office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit outstanding landlord, sanitation or tax certificates; appeal municipal assessment; re-apply once inspections are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolution, bank account opening and SBP license pre-application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting and minute the first board resolution. Appoint officers, the AML compliance officer and, if desired, begin the SBP pre-examination for the electronic-money license. The officers are then authorized to open corporate bank accounts and to submit the formal authorization package to the SBP when the institutional business plan is ready.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Supplement due-diligence documents upon SBP request; amend the corporate object or capital structure by notarial modification if required by the qualification process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá – Dirección de Licencias/Autorizaciones, jointly with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero for AML/CFT vetting
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Empresa Emisora de Dinero Electrónico (electronic-money institution / digital wallet issuer) under Ley 15 de 2021 and SBP implementing regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Impact Registration (Registro de Impacto Ambiental) for the office/back-office facility; full EIA Report not required for a non-industrial financial technology operation with no new infrastructure, hazardous effluent or wastewater discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC point-source discharge is expected. If backup generators or fuel storage are installed, comply with MiAMBIENTE air-quality emission limits, fuel-handling safety standards, municipal solid-waste disposal rules, and the general water-protection provisions of Ley 41 de 1998.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Benemerito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural load and occupancy inspection by the Municipal Engineer's Office; occupational medicine and public-health clearance from MINSA for the office; and emergency response plan review by SINAPROC.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama; online portal: SIME – Sistema Integrado de Mejoramiento de la Administración Tributaria (https://sime.com.pa); taxpayer e-services: SIRUC – Sistema de Información y Registro Único de Contribuyentes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity (including a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima with foreign shareholders) must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) from DGI prior to commencing taxable activities in Panama. Procedure: (1) file notarized certificate of incorporation and registered bylaws with the Public Registry; (2) apply for an Aviso de Operación (business permit) from the relevant municipality; (3) register with DGI via the SIRUC or an authorized notary/agent using the DGI-RA-01 form, providing corporate documents, proof of legal representative's ID (cédula/passport), and a local fiscal address; (4) obtain RUC certificate and activate the SIME online account; (5) for a licensed EMI (electronic money institution) with virtual IBAN issuance activity, present the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (SBP) license or letter of no-objection for the Fintech license, and file the AML/KYC compliance annex. Processing time is normally 5–10 business days. Non-resident shareholders are permitted; a local statutory agent is mandatory for the S.A. entity. A foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Panama may require a simplified RUC only if deriving Panamanian-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Panamanian law. Taxation is territorial: a Panamanian S.A. is taxed only on Panamanian-source income and not on worldwide income. Available elections include: (a) election to apply the Small Taxpayer Regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) for annual gross income up to B/.300,000; (b) election under Law 41 of 2007 and Executive Decree 153 of 2005 for Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime, enabling a reduced effective tax rate and whatever-case exemptions for qualifying EMIs; (c) election for tax consolidation of affiliated entities under DGI-approved rules; (d) election for foreign tax credit under tax treaties (limited to specific double taxation agreements). Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized; Panama does not apply OECD BEPS hybrid mismatch rules as national law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Value Added Tax equivalent)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold for ITBMS registration; any person or entity habitually performing taxable acts (including digital and financial services) in Panama must register. A 'Small Taxpayer' simplified threshold applies to persons or entities with annual gross income of up to B/.300,000, allowing simplified filing and payment; the threshold is B/.300,000 Panamanian Balboas (B/.1.00 = USD 1.00).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all registered taxpayers on a phased implementation schedule. Issuers must transmit structured electronic invoices (XML format) to the DGI platform in near-real time for validation and digital stamping; the DGI returns a unique authorization number (Código de Trazabilidad o Autorización) before the receipt can be legally issued to the client. The platform supports B2B and B2C models, enforced via SIME's 'Facturación Electrónica de Panamá' module. Financial entities, including EMI licensees, must use the sector-specific e-invoice scheme with extended fields for fees, virtual IBAN transactions, and electronic money reserve evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (a) exports of tangible goods physically leaving Panama, and (b) services sold to non-residents that are performed, used, or exploited outside Panama, including offshore payment processing, digital wallet administration, virtual IBAN issuance, and cross-border fintech services (under Article 1565 of the Panama Tax Code and regulatory amendments). To claim 0% ITBMS, the EMI must establish the export nature of the service via a written contract with a non-resident recipient, plus proof that the service is not consumed in Panama. Direct transfer of goods or services to a Panamanian resident, even if booked as 'export', is disallowed. Export services must be invoiced using the DGI e-invoice export code; the corresponding input VAT (on local costs) is creditable and any excess is refundable through DGI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Declaración Única Aduanera) for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill with proof of departure from Panamanian territory
Copy of the commercial invoice evidencing the export transaction
Proof of receipt and acceptance by the foreign buyer or service recipient
Payment certificate or inward remittance evidence (bank or SWIFT records) in the name of the Panamanian exporter
For electronic money services: SBP licensed EMI approval and KYC/destination report evidencing the non-resident status of the counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama imposes substantial audit scrutiny on export zero-rating claims. If DGI finds fraudulent, false, or unsubstantiated export documentation, it may retrospectively reverse the zero-rating, levy the 7% ITBMS plus surcharge, late-payment interest, and a fine ranging from 100% to 300% of the omitted tax; criminal penalties for tax fraud include imprisonment under Panama's Tax Code (Articles 783–785) and the general criminal code for aggravated and repeated offenses. Additionally, the SBP may suspend or revoke the EMI license, and the financial institution's directors and compliance officers may be subject to personal liability and administrative sanctions. Under Panamanian law, failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may be considered an indication of unrealized export; the tax administration may treat the transaction as non-exported if no reasonable explanation is provided, resulting in the same recapture and penalty regime. DGI applies a robust documentary and economic substance review for electronic money institutions due to the high-risk classification of digital wallet and virtual IBAN business.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as banking, payment-systems and financial-license regulator; Banco Nacional de Panamá as state fiscal agent and clearing bank; no traditional central bank exists, and the U.S. dollar is the de facto legal tender with balboa only as nominal coinage.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized and open-economy monetary system with no exchange-control law, no prior-approval mechanism, and no compulsory buy/sell rates. Current-account items (goods, services, royalties, remittances) and capital-account items (equity injections, intercompany loans, foreign direct investment, portfolio flows) are freely convertible because transactions are executed in USD. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are unrestricted in FX terms; they are subject only to Panama's territorial dividend withholding regime and standard corporate income taxation. The material FX exposure for an electronic money institution is limited to non-USD balances such as EUR, CNY, COP, MXN and BRL held for cross-border disbursement, which can be converted through licensed local banks without regulatory filing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Panama. Export receipts and all other foreign-currency earnings may be held indefinitely in USD or any convertible currency, transferred abroad without restriction, and never require conversion into balboa. There is no prescribed repatriation timeline for Panama-incorporated entities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: State-owned fiscal agent; operational and clearing account in USD
Operational account, segregated reserve escrow, and virtual IBAN omnibus settlement account
Operational USD account plus multicurrency treasury account for EUR, COP and MXN
Treasury and liquidity account with U.S. correspondent clearing
Digital wallet float, card-program settlement and client funds escrow account
Private banking and sponsor-banking account for high-volume payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Panama Law 23 of 2015 and the SBP Innovation Hub permit supervised non-bank electronic payment issuers to maintain USD settlement accounts with licensed Panamanian banks, but offshore digital EMIs are not granted direct access to U.S. Fedwire, CHIPS or ACH systems. A foreign EMI must contract a licensed local sponsor bank and may not join the SBP national ACH or RTGS settlement circuits without a full financial-company license. SBP restricts outsourcing of KYC functions to unregulated third parties; an approved outsourcing model with UAF registration and data-residency safeguards is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interviews are the prevailing standard for ultimate beneficial owners, directors and signatories when opening corporate accounts at SBP-regulated banks. Remote opening is permitted only on a case-by-case basis where a notarized and apostilled power of attorney is lodged, the resident agent certifies the corporate existence, identity verification is conducted through recorded video sessions, and the bank applies enhanced due diligence because the client is a licensed fintech. Physical board attendance becomes practically unavoidable for a first-generation S.A. with non-resident owners, and at least one local signatory is normally required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector classification: virtual IBAN aggregation and e-money reserve management without a recognized banking or payments license in the residence jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SBP-issued electronic payment instrument license; comprehensive AML/CFT compliance manual; UAF registration certificate; compliance committee minutes; board-approved business plan with reserve-management and safeguarding policy; opening balance sheet and audited capital evidence; board resolution appointing a permanent UAF compliance officer; monthly transaction-velocity and wallet-float forecasts

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: S.A. with nominee directors or UBOs located in higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of registration in Panama's ultimate beneficial ownership registry under Law 254 of 2021; twelve-month source-of-wealth statement; apostilled passports and utility-address proof for every UBO above 10%; two independent bank references from licensed foreign institutions; sworn affidavit of commercial substance; legal opinion from reputable Panamanian counsel confirming no bearer-share or nominee-control risks

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Money-remittance red flags: cross-border wires with missing purpose codes, aggregator or conduit patterns, or incomplete remitter information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual payment-message policy adopting ISO 20022 structured data; SWIFT purpose-code and remitter-information declaration; transaction-monitoring rulebook approved by the money-laundering reporting officer; counterparty due-diligence inventory covering every sponsored client; sanctions and PEP screening logs generated in real time; UAF Travel Rule compliant originator and beneficiary records for every transfer above USD 1,000

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate expected turnover relative to declared paid-in capital of the newly formed S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Collateralized liquidity schedule and capital-adequacy reconciliation against SBP minimum-equity requirements; monthly liquidity stress tests; independent audit report; external valuation of reserve assets; treasury policy demonstrating segregation of client funds in dedicated escrow accounts; transaction-forecast model showing alignment of wallet float with actual clearing capacity

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder-loan proceeds are wired via SWIFT MT103 followed by MT202 COV from the overseas sponsor bank into the segregated USD capital account at a licensed Panamanian bank. The instruction must name PA_CORP as beneficiary and include the purpose narrative 'Shareholder capital injection / e-money reserve funding'. The remitter must be the disclosed UBO or a regulated financial institution, and the supporting package must contain board minutes, intercompany loan agreement, source-of-funds letter, notarized capital-subscription consent and UAF Travel Rule records. No exchange-control authorization or central-bank formality is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound commercial settlement uses SWIFT MT101 and MT103 payment messages cleared through the Panamanian bank's U.S. correspondent network, principally CHIPS and Fedwire. Full-value and high-amount transfers require MT202 COV with explicit purpose-code annotations. Trade finance is supported by irrevocable documentary commercial letters of credit under UCP 600, opened by MT700 and confirmed by sponsor banks with MT754 confirmations. Local Panamanian client payouts settle through the SBP ACH and RTGS systems, with daily MT900/MT910 statements and nostro reconciliation forming the core liquidity-control discipline.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR and USD/CNY spot contracts executed with the sponsor bank
Deliverable FX forwards in USD/EUR and USD/CNH maturing up to twelve months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP, USD/MXN and USD/BRL booked through the New York or London trading desk
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps in USD/EUR and USD/CNH under an ISDA 2002 master agreement with investment-grade dealer banks
Plain-vanilla European-style currency options on USD against EUR, CNY, COP and MXN as cash-flow protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Corporate Entity (Pago de Anualidad / Reporte Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the fourth month following the quarter of the incorporation anniversary: Jan–Mar incorporations due 31 May; Apr–Jun incorporations due 31 Aug; Jul–Sep incorporations due 30 Nov; Oct–Dec incorporations due 28/29 Feb.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% surcharge on the unpaid annual fee plus arrears interest; the entity is marked 'incumplida' in the Registry; three consecutive years of non-payment authorize administrative strike-off and dissolution of the S.A. with loss of corporate capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Declaration (Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December fiscal year-end: due on or before 31 March of the following year; for fiscal years closing on any other date: due within three months after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine equal to 15% of the tax owed plus 1.5% monthly interest on arrears; continued default may trigger an ex officio assessment, asset seizures, and denial of 'paz y salvo' clearance for banking and government operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Beneficial Owner (FBO) Annual Declaration — Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (Law 254 of 2021)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Registro Público de Panamá (UBO electronic portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation submitted concurrently with the Anualidad payment window; any share transfer or UBO ownership change must be reported within 30 calendar days from the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Law 254 of 2021, up to B/.100,000 for serious omissions; the entity may lose good standing, with registration, notarial, and banking operations blocked until compliance is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and SBP Supervisory Compliance Report (Electronic Money Institution License)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements and the regulatory compliance package must be filed within 120 days after the fiscal year-end, in accordance with the SBP reporting calendar for licensed e-money institutions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly monetary penalties imposed by the SBP for delayed submission; persistent non-compliance is grounds for suspension or revocation of the e-money license and mandatory cessation of payment and digital-wallet operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance Report and Risk Self-Assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual AML/CFT report and institutional risk self-assessment filed by 31 March following the reporting year; suspicious transaction and currency transaction reports are submitted continuously as prescribed by Law 23 of 2015.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to B/.500,000 under Law 23 of 2015 for AML reporting failures; possible designation as a non-compliant or high-risk institution; criminal liability for compliance officers; license revocation and liquidation of e-money reserves.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all SBP-licensed electronic money institutions irrespective of revenue; for general Panama S.A. entities, audited financial statements by a licensed public accountant are required when annual gross revenue or total assets exceed B/.300,000 (Executive Decree 170 of 1993) and for issuers under the securities market law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the binding framework for financial institutions and public-interest entities; unlisted small and medium enterprises may apply IFRS for SMEs; compliance is supervised by the Consejo Técnico de Auditoría y Contabilidad (CTAC).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 254 of 2021 requires every Panama S.A. to maintain a current Final Beneficial Owner (FBO) declaration in the electronic UBO register of the Registro Público; the declaration is confirmed annually together with the Anualidad, and any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the company's share register and reported to the UBO portal within 30 calendar days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Transferencias de Acciones (Share Transfer Ledger)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 – $550 per annum for licensed registered agent and registered office services in Panama City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 – $24,000 per annum for a certified audit firm registered with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The territorial system taxes only Panama-source income. A licensed EMI is taxable on Panama-source fee income, IBAN maintenance fees and local float investment returns, while interchange fees derived from foreign SEPA rails and other revenue attributable to purely foreign-source activity are excludable. No general CIT holiday exists for EMIs. The 25% rate is partially mitigated by (i) full territorial exclusion of foreign-source profits without CFC rules, (ii) a 1.5% minimum advance 'dividend tax' on net taxable income creditable against the 10% dividend withholding tax, and (iii) VAT/ITBMS exemption on exported B2B services. Deductibility of foreign-parent fees is subject to the arm's length standard and the 3:1 thin-capitalisation ceiling.
